core_obligations: Use the two power containments to build a map of inverse systems M/I^nM to M/J^{floor(n/c)}M and a map of inverse systems in the other direction M/J^mM to M/I^{floor(m/d)}M (proof lines 23035-23038).
Check that the two systems are mutually inverse on the completions, which identifies the I-adic and J-adic completions of every R-module (proof line 23038).
Read off that an R-module is I-adically complete exactly when it is J-adically complete (statement lines 23030-23031).
proof_roadmap: Turn the containment of a power of one ideal in the other into a map of the quotient towers in each direction (proof lines 23034-23037).
Pass to the inverse limits and observe the two maps are inverse to each other (proof lines 23037-23039).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if ideals I, J of a ring R satisfy I^c contained in J and J^d contained in I for positive integers c, d, then the I-adic and J-adic completions of every R-module agree, so adic completeness is the same notion for the two ideals (statement lines 23022-23032). The proof does not compare the two topologies directly or construct the identity as a limit of identities: it writes down a map of inverse systems M/I^nM to M/J^{floor(n/c)}M from the first containment and the symmetric one from the second, and observes that they are mutually inverse on the completions (proof lines 23034-23039). The floors that convert a multiplicative containment into a map of towers are the substance, and the author records exactly that step. H2.
